title: Minimize application impact during fleet maintenance
creator: Evan Zhao
description: Goal: build an automated maintenance conductor that performs node drains, software upgrades, and hardware rotations with minimal customer-visible impact while preserving throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers. Scope: maintenance window scheduling, controlled drain ramp, capacity-preservation tokens (temporary reserved throughput), pre-warm node pools, and automatic rollback triggers. Out of scope for this ticket: UI features in Console (separate PM ticket) and private on-prem packaging steps.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Evan Zhao: Initial proposal drafted. Key constraints: we must avoid global autoscaler oscillation during rolling upgrades, and ensure throughput guarantees for Gold customers are honored even when up to 25% of a shard is draining.

2026-02-25 - Marisol Rivera: Reviewed proposal. Requested acceptance criteria tied to telemetry (p95/p99 latency, error rate, tokens/sec) and a synthetic canary run plan. Also requested explicit backoff policy for multi-region rollouts.

2026-03-04 - Eng lead (Priya Nair): Implementation approach validated. Decided to implement a lightweight admission controller that issues "preservation tokens" to routes pinned to a fleet so the router can throttle non-critical traffic during maintenance windows.

2026-03-09 - QA (Daniel Kim): Ran first integration test in staging. Observed a transient 0.6% error increase when pre-warm nodes come up; flagged to add gradual ramp for pre-warm traffic drain. Created follow-up test to iterate on drain step size.

2026-03-12 - Marisol Rivera: Design review complete. Added links to runbook and rollout playbook. Assigned Marisol as release owner for canary in eu-west-1. Next: finalize autoscaler invariants and merge feature-flag gated PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Automated maintenance conductor can schedule and execute a rolling maintenance across a single shard with configurable concurrency (default: 2 nodes concurrently) without manual intervention

During a simulated maintenance where 25% of capacity is draining, Gold-tier customers maintain at least 90% of their baseline peak throughput and p99 latency stays within SLA (+20ms tolerance), as measured by dedicated synthetic traffic
No more than 0.5% of user requests fail or return 5xx due to maintenance when the conductor is active; any higher error rate triggers automatic pause and rollback
Pre-warm pools reduce cold-start tail latency by >= 30% in synthetic runs and do not cause autoscaler thrash (no more than 2 scale events per 10 minutes observed in staging),
Observability: Console dashboard exposes maintenance window, nodes draining, preserved throughput tokens, and a red/amber/green health status per shard
Operational runbook exists with explicit BCDR steps, and a canary rollout plan validated in eu-west-1 before global execution
implementation_notes: Design an admission controller that can mark specific routes as 'preserve-throughput' and allocate a preservation token bucket which the router consults when deciding to admit or redirect traffic
Introduce a drain-state machine per node: DRAIN_SCHEDULED -> PREPARE (pre-warm replacement) -> SLOW_DRAIN (priority traffic retained, best-effort background evictions) -> FAST_DRAIN -> OFFLINE
Throttle background eviction and rebalancing work during maintenance windows to avoid compounding load on healthy nodes
Autoscaler invariants: honor preservation tokens by treating preserved capacity as 'soft cushion' that is only borrowed when safety thresholds (error rate tolerant) are met
Implement gradual pre-warm ramp: create ephemeral warm instances, attach small fraction of traffic, ramp based on latency/error signals before moving full traffic
Expose new metrics: maintenance.node_drain_progress, maintenance.preserved_tokens_used, maintenance.prewarm_success_rate, maintenance.rolling_error_delta
Feature gate the conductor behind runtime flag and iterative rollout with canaries; add kill-switch to immediately abort ongoing maintenance and re-instate pre-maintenance routing
Add end-to-end tests: synthetic traffic for throughput-preservation, failure injection for pre-warm glitches, and autoscaler stability tests
